turns.speaker: James
turns.text: Hey David, how's the checkout PR coming along?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Pretty good. The feature is done, but my branch is behind develop.

turns.speaker: James
turns.text: How far behind are you?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: About six commits. I also noticed that two of the checkout files have changed on develop.

turns.speaker: James
turns.text: Okay. Do you expect any conflicts?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Yeah, probably. Both branches changed the checkout controller.

turns.speaker: James
turns.text: Got it. Do you want to rebase the branch onto develop?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Yeah, I think that's the better option here. Is that okay with you?

turns.speaker: James
turns.text: Yep. Just make sure you run the tests after resolving the conflicts.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Sure. I'll rebase first, resolve the conflicts locally, and run the checkout tests.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: How much time do you think that will take?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Probably an hour or so, assuming there aren't any unexpected conflicts.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Okay. Does that put the PR at risk for today's review?

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: I don't think so. I should be able to update the PR this afternoon.

turns.speaker: James
turns.text: Sounds good. One thing to watch out for is the frontend changes in the same flow.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Right. I'll check those after I resolve the backend conflict.

turns.speaker: James
turns.text: Perfect. And don't force-push unless you're sure the branch is only yours.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Got it. It's my feature branch, so that should be fine.

turns.speaker: Sarah
turns.text: Okay. Let us know once it's ready for review.

turns.speaker: David
turns.text: Sure. I'll post an update in the PR when the tests pass.

turns.speaker: James
turns.text: Great.
